name: Masala Egg Rice
description: A fragrant, comforting one-pan rice dish tossed with scrambled eggs, sweet caramelized onions, juicy tomatoes, and warm spices.
ingredient_details: 2 cups cooked rice (day-old rice works best)
1/2 tsp garam masala or curry powder
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan or wok over medium heat.
Add finely chopped onions and green chilli; sauté for 3-4 minutes until onions turn translucent and slightly golden.
Add diced tomatoes, turmeric powder, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tomatoes soften into a juicy masala.
Push the veggies to one side of the pan and pour in the beaten eggs. Scramble gently for 1-2 minutes until soft curds form.
Add the cooked rice and garam masala. Toss everything gently on high heat for 2 minutes until evenly coated and steaming hot.
Garnish with fresh coriander if desired and serve hot with yogurt or ketchup.
tips: Using chilled leftover rice prevents the grains from breaking while tossing.
To make it less spicy, discard the seeds from the green chilli or substitute with a pinch of mild paprika.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
description: Fast wok-tossed street-style fried rice loaded with crunchy veggies, aromatic garlic, and savory soy sauce.
ingredient_details: 1/2 cup finely chopped capsicum / bell pepper
steps: Heat oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat until smoking.
Add minced garlic and onions; stir-fry rapidly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toss in carrots and capsicum; stir-fry on high flame for 2 minutes to keep them crisp.
Add the cold cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with your spatula.
Drizzle soy sauce, black pepper, and a pinch of salt around the edges of the pan.
Toss continuously on high heat for 2 minutes until well combined, smoky, and heated through.
tips: High heat is the secret to authentic restaurant-style fried rice flavor.
Add a splash of vinegar or chili oil at the end for extra zing.

name: Quick Garlic Tomato Pasta
description: Al dente penne smothered in a rich, garlicky crushed tomato sauce finished with dried oregano and cheese.
ingredient_details: 3 ripe tomatoes, pureed or finely diced
1 tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
Salt and red chili flakes to taste
steps: Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook pasta for 9-10 minutes until al dente; reserve 1/4 cup pasta water and drain.
In a separate pan, warm olive oil over medium-low heat. Add garlic slices and cook gently for 1 minute until golden.
Add onions and sauté until soft, then stir in the tomatoes, oregano, salt, and chili flakes.
Simmer the sauce for 6-8 minutes until thickened and glossy.
Add drained pasta and reserved pasta water to the pan. Toss vigorously for 1 minute to coat pasta evenly.
Top with grated cheese and serve immediately.
tips: Always salt your pasta boiling water generously—it seasons the pasta from the inside out.
The reserved starchy pasta water emulsifies the sauce into a silky restaurant finish.

name: Classic Bombay Veg Grilled Sandwich
description: Crispy golden toasted bread stuffed with spiced potato, tomato, onion, cucumber slices, and melted cheese.
ingredient_details: 4 slices of bread (white, brown, or multigrain)
steps: Lay out bread slices and lightly spread butter (and green chutney if you have it).
Layer slices of boiled potato, cucumber, tomato, and onion on two bread slices.
Sprinkle chaat masala over the vegetables and place cheese on top.
Cover with the remaining bread slices and butter the outer sides.
Toast in a sandwich maker, grill pan, or regular tawa on medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Slice diagonally and enjoy with tomato ketchup.
tips: Toasting on low-medium flame ensures the cheese melts completely before the bread burns.
Boil potatoes in advance and store them in the fridge for instant 5-minute sandwiches.

name: Spicy Paneer Tikka Wrap
description: Soft flatbread or tortilla rolled around pan-seared paneer cubes marinated in yogurt and spices with crunchy onions.
steps: In a bowl, mix curd, red chilli powder, garam masala, salt, and 1 tsp oil.
Coat paneer cubes in this spiced marinade and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat remaining oil in a skillet. Sear the paneer cubes for 4-5 minutes until golden on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, toss sliced onions and capsicum for 1 minute over high heat to keep them crunchy.
Warm the rotis or wraps on the tawa.
Assemble by placing spiced paneer cubes and crunchy veggies down the center of each wrap, roll tightly, and serve.
tips: Do not overcook paneer or it will turn rubbery—3 to 5 minutes is plenty!
A squeeze of fresh lemon juice before rolling adds an irresistible street-food tang.

name: Street-Style Egg Hakka Noodles
description: Tossed noodles with shredded cabbage, carrots, spring onions, and fluffy scrambled egg with soy and vinegar.
steps: Boil noodles according to package instructions (about 4 minutes). Drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with 1 tsp oil.
Heat 1/2 tbsp oil in a pan, pour in beaten eggs, scramble softly for 1 minute, and set aside.
Heat remaining 1 tbsp oil on high heat. Add minced garlic, onions, and carrots; toss rapidly for 2 minutes.
Add cooked noodles, scrambled eggs, soy sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and salt.
Using two spatulas, toss everything together on high heat for 2 minutes until steaming.
Serve hot with chili sauce.
tips: Rinsing cooked noodles under cold water stops the cooking process and prevents mushiness.
Add sliced green chillies for an Indian-Chinese spicy kick.

name: Homestyle Dal Tadka & Rice
description: Comforting yellow lentils tempered with ghee, cumin seeds, garlic, and fresh coriander, served over warm steamed rice.
ingredient_details: 3/4 cup toor or yellow moong dal
steps: Wash dal and cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and salt (pressure cook for 3-4 whistles or simmer in a pot for 20 mins).
In a small pan, heat ghee or oil for the tadka (tempering).
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle. Add crushed garlic and fry until fragrant and lightly brown.
Add onions and fry until light brown, then add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Pour this aromatic tadka into the cooked dal and stir well. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve warm over fresh steamed rice.
tips: Yellow moong dal cooks fastest without needing a pressure cooker.
Ghee in the tadka elevates the aroma significantly compared to oil.

name: Fluffy Masala Omelette & Toast
description: Classic Indian road-side spiced omelette with onions, tomatoes, and green chillies served with buttered toasted bread.
ingredient_details: Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: In a bowl, whisk eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli, turmeric, salt, and pepper until frothy.
Melt 1/2 tsp butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Pour in the whisked egg mixture, tilting the pan so it spreads evenly into a circle.
Cook for 2 minutes until the bottom is set and edges lift easily.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1 minute until cooked through and golden.
Toast bread in the same pan with remaining butter and serve with the hot omelette.
tips: Whisking eggs vigorously for 45 seconds incorporates air, making the omelette soft and fluffy.
Keep onions finely chopped so they cook through quickly.

name: Quick Kanda Poha
description: Light, fluffy flattened rice seasoned with mustard seeds, onions, crunchy peanuts, and fresh lemon juice.
ingredient_details: 1.5 cups medium or thick poha (flattened rice)
1 small boiled or finely diced potato
steps: Rinse poha in a colander under running water for 30 seconds; drain completely and let rest so it fluffs up.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add peanuts and sauté for 1 minute until golden, then add onions, green chilli, and diced potato.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until onions are soft and potatoes are tender.
Add turmeric powder and salt, then gently add the softened poha.
Toss gently on low heat for 2-3 minutes. Turn off heat, drizzle lemon juice, and serve warm.
tips: Do not soak poha in a bowl of water—just rinse in a sieve to avoid turning it mushy.
Peanuts add a satisfying crunch and bonus plant protein.

name: Vegetable Rava Upma
description: Savory South Indian semolina porridge cooked with mustard seeds, ginger, onions, carrots, and green chillies.
steps: Dry roast rava in a pan on medium-low flame for 3-4 minutes until warm and fragrant; set aside.
Heat oil in the pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add ginger, green chilli, chopped onions, and carrots. Sauté for 3 minutes until soft.
Add 2.5 cups water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the flame. Slowly pour the roasted rava in a continuous stream with one hand while stirring continuously with the other to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2 minutes until water is absorbed and upma is soft and fluffy.
tips: Pouring the semolina gradually while stirring prevents any lump formation.
A spoonful of ghee on top right before serving makes it incredibly comforting.

name: One-Pot Easy Chole (Chickpea Curry)
description: Rich, spicy North Indian chickpea curry infused with ginger, garlic, tomato gravy, and chole masala.
ingredient_details: 1.5 cups boiled or canned chickpeas (kabuli chana)
1 large onion, pureed or finely chopped
1.5 tbsp chole masala or garam masala
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and fry for 5-6 minutes until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute until the raw aroma disappears.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, chole masala, and salt. Cook until oil starts separating from the masala.
Add the boiled chickpeas and 1 cup water. Mash a few chickpeas with the back of a spoon to thicken the gravy.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes on low heat so the chickpeas absorb all the spices. Serve with rice or bread.
tips: Mashing 10% of the chickpeas creates a thick, restaurant-style gravy naturally without cornstarch.
Canned chickpeas save 30 minutes of soaking and boiling time.

name: Cheesy Golden Garlic Bread
description: Crispy toasted bread slices slathered with rich garlic herb butter and topped with gooey melted cheese.
ingredient_details: 4 slices of bread (baguette, sourdough, or sandwich bread)
1/2 cup grated mozzarella or processed cheese
steps: In a small bowl, mix softened butter, minced garlic, and oregano into a spreadable garlic butter.
Spread garlic butter generously on one side of each bread slice.
Place bread slices on a preheated tawa/skillet buttered side down for 1 minute until crisp.
Flip, heap grated cheese on top, sprinkle with chili flakes, and cover with a lid on low flame for 2-3 minutes until cheese melts.
Cut into fingers and serve hot.
tips: Covering the pan with a lid is essential for melting cheese without an oven.
Use softened room-temperature butter rather than melted butter for the best spread.

name: Creamy Tomato Soup & Croutons
description: Smooth, velvety roasted tomato soup seasoned with garlic, black pepper, and topped with crunchy bread croutons.
ingredient_details: 4 large ripe red tomatoes, roughly chopped
Salt and sugar to balance acidity
steps: Heat butter in a pot; add garlic and onion, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, 1 cup water, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until tomatoes are mushy.
Blend the tomato mixture until smooth using an immersion blender or mixer; strain if you prefer a silky texture.
Return soup to pot, stir in milk or cream, and simmer on low for 2 minutes. Adjust salt and sugar.
Cut bread into cubes and toast in a dry pan until crunchy croutons form.
Ladle hot soup into bowls and top with crispy croutons.
tips: A pinch of sugar cuts through tomato acidity and brings out natural sweetness.
Stir the milk in on low heat so it doesn't curdle.

name: Quick Aloo Jeera (Cumin Spiced Potatoes)
description: Crispy pan-fried potato cubes tossed with roasted cumin seeds, green chillies, turmeric, and fresh cilantro.
ingredient_details: 2 medium boiled potatoes, peeled and cubed
1/2 tsp amchur (dry mango powder) or lemon juice
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle until dark golden and fragrant.
Add chopped green chilli and turmeric powder; stir for 10 seconds.
Add cubed potatoes and salt. Toss gently to coat in the cumin oil.
Roast on medium flame for 5-6 minutes, flipping occasionally until the potato edges turn crispy and golden.
Sprinkle amchur or squeeze lemon juice, toss once more, and serve hot.
tips: Let boiled potatoes cool completely before slicing so they don't break into mash.
Pairs wonderfully with toast, paratha, or dal rice.

name: One-Pot Vegetable Pulao
description: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with whole spices, sliced onions, carrots, and peas for an effortless one-pot meal.
ingredient_details: 1.5 cups basmati rice (rinsed and soaked for 15 mins)
steps: Heat oil or ghee in a deep pot or pressure cooker.
Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, and cloves; let them crackle.
Add sliced onions and sauté for 4 minutes until light golden.
Toss in carrots and green peas; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add drained rice, garam masala, salt, and 3 cups of water.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork and serve.
tips: Do not stir rice excessively while cooking or the long grains will snap.
Serve with plain curd or boondi raita for a complete dinner.

name: Chili Garlic Paneer Stir-Fry
description: Tender paneer cubes tossed in a fiery garlic and soy glaze with crunchy bell peppers and onions.
ingredient_details: 1 tbsp red chilli sauce or sriracha
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add paneer cubes and shallow fry for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden; transfer to a plate.
In the same hot pan, add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add diced onions and capsicum; stir-fry briskly on high flame for 2 minutes to keep them crisp.
Add soy sauce, red chilli sauce, black pepper, and 2 tbsp water to create a sauce.
Toss the pan-fried paneer cubes into the sauce until glazed and piping hot.
tips: Soak paneer in warm water for 5 minutes before cooking if it feels firm from the fridge.
Makes a delicious high-protein student dinner ready in just 15 minutes.

name: Student Special 20-Min Egg Curry
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy flavored with ginger, garlic, and garam masala.
ingredient_details: 4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and lightly pierced
steps: Heat 1/2 tbsp oil in a pan with a pinch of turmeric and salt; lightly roll the boiled eggs for 2 minutes until blistered and golden, then remove.
Add remaining oil to the pan. Add chopped onions and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until the tomato masala releases oil.
Add 3/4 cup water, bring to a simmer, and slide in the golden boiled eggs.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the curry thickens. Sprinkle garam masala and serve with rice or bread.
tips: Pricking eggs with a fork prevents them from bursting when frying and lets the curry soak into the whites.
Keep hard-boiled eggs in your fridge for ultra-fast weekday protein meals.

name: Upgraded Ramen with Veggies & Egg
description: The ultimate student staple upgraded with sautéed onions, tomatoes, crunchy veggies, and a fried or poached egg.
steps: Heat oil in a small pot or pan. Add onions and green chilli; sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook for 1 minute until softened.
Pour in 1.5 cups water and add the noodle seasoning packet; bring to a boil.
Break in the noodles. Cook on medium heat for 2 minutes.
Crack an egg right in the center of the bubbling noodles. Cover with a lid and simmer for 2 minutes until egg white is set and yolk is jammy.
Serve hot right out of the bowl.
tips: Covering the pan lets the steam gently poach the egg right on top of the noodles.
Add a slice of cheese on top for an indulgent cafe-style creamy ramen.

name: High-Protein Chaat Chickpea Salad
description: No-cook zesty chickpea salad tossed with crisp cucumbers, ripe tomatoes, red onions, lemon juice, and tangy chaat masala.
ingredient_details: 1.5 cups boiled or canned chickpeas, rinsed
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Add rinsed chickpeas to a large mixing bowl.
Add diced cucumber, tomato, and finely chopped onion.
Sprinkle chaat masala, a pinch of black pepper, and salt.
Drizzle fresh lemon juice over everything.
Toss thoroughly to combine all flavors and serve immediately or chill in the fridge.
tips: Zero cooking required! Perfect for busy study days or a post-workout snack.
Add diced boiled potato or roasted peanuts for extra texture.

name: 5-Minute Chocolate Mug Cake
description: Single-serving rich, molten chocolate cake mixed right inside a mug and cooked in under 2 minutes in the microwave.
ingredient_details: 1 tbsp vegetable oil or melted butter
steps: In a microwave-safe mug, whisk together flour, sugar, cocoa powder, and baking powder with a fork.
Add milk and oil; stir until a smooth batter forms with no dry flour lumps.
Drop a chunk of chocolate into the center of the batter.
Microwave on high for 70-80 seconds until the top has risen and looks set.
Let cool for 1 minute before digging in.
tips: Do not overcook or the cake will dry out—it should look slightly moist on top when done.
Top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream for a real dessert treat.

name: Cheesy Black Bean Quesadilla
description: Crispy golden flour tortilla filled with seasoned mashed beans, sweet corn, melted cheddar cheese, and cumin.
ingredient_details: 1/2 cup canned black beans or boiled rajma, lightly mashed
steps: In a small bowl, mix mashed beans with cumin, diced onion, and a pinch of salt.
Place tortilla flat and spread cheese over one half.
Spread the seasoned bean mixture on top of the cheese, then top with a little more cheese.
Fold the tortilla in half over the filling to make a semi-circle.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; toast the quesadilla for 3 minutes per side until golden brown and cheese melts.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa or yogurt.
tips: Putting cheese both below and above the beans glues the quesadilla together perfectly.
Leftover boiled rajma makes an exceptional filling.

name: Korean Style Spicy Fried Egg Rice
description: Steaming bowl of warm rice topped with a crispy fried egg, savory soy-sesame drizzle, and spicy chili oil.
steps: Heat cooking oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Crack in the egg and fry until edges are deeply browned and crispy, with the yolk still runny.
Place warm rice in your serving bowl.
In a tiny dish, mix soy sauce, grated garlic, sesame oil, and chili flakes.
Slide the crispy fried egg on top of the warm rice.
Drizzle the garlic-soy-chili sauce over the egg and rice, break the yolk, and mix everything together thoroughly.
tips: The runny yolk blends with soy sauce and sesame oil to create a luscious rich glaze on each grain of rice.
Takes only 8 minutes and costs pennies.

name: Crispy Spiced Potato Bread Rolls
description: Classic Indian evening snack: bread slices stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes, rolled and pan-toasted until crackly.
ingredient_details: 4 slices of white or brown bread
steps: In a bowl, mix mashed potatoes with onions, green chilli, turmeric, chaat masala, and salt.
Shape the potato mixture into 4 cylindrical logs.
Dip a bread slice in a shallow bowl of water for 2 seconds; immediately squeeze between your palms to remove excess water.
Place a potato log in the center of the moist bread, roll and seal edges tightly to form a neat roll.
Heat oil in a pan and pan-fry the rolls, turning frequently for 5-6 minutes until deep golden brown and crunchy.
Serve hot with tomato sauce.
tips: Press the wet bread firmly between both palms so it turns pliable and seals without tearing.
Pan-frying gives the same crunch as deep frying with 80% less oil.

name: Street-Style Paneer Bhurji & Toast
description: Crumbled paneer cooked with sautéed onions, tomatoes, green chillies, and fragrant spices, served over buttery toast.
steps: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and green chilli; sauté for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes until soft and pulpy.
Add crumbled paneer and toss gently on medium heat for 2-3 minutes until heated through and coated.
Do not overcook the paneer so it stays juicy and tender.
Toast bread slices with a little butter on a tawa; spoon hot paneer bhurji over the toast and enjoy.
tips: Crumbling paneer unevenly with hands gives the dish authentic texture rather than grating it fine.
A splash of milk keeps the bhurji wonderfully moist.

name: Creamy Peanut Butter & Banana Oats
description: Warm, creamy rolled oats cooked in milk, naturally sweetened with sliced banana, and topped with rich peanut butter.
steps: In a small pot, combine oats, milk, and a tiny pinch of salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally for 3-4 minutes until thick and creamy.
Turn off the heat and stir in half of the sliced banana (it will soften into the warm oats).
Transfer to a breakfast bowl.
Top with remaining banana slices, a generous dollop of peanut butter, and a drizzle of honey.
tips: A pinch of salt enhances the natural nutty sweetness of oats and peanut butter.
Can be made in the microwave in just 2 minutes on high power.
